origins.section: -Xss Sets How Many Frames Fit, So Recursion as Deep as the Data Fails on Large Input
OutOfMemoryError Is Thrown by Whichever Allocation Fails, Not by the Code That Filled the Heap
An Object Costs a Header Plus Its Fields, Rounded Up to 8 Bytes; a Reference Costs 4 Bytes Below 32 GB
Escape Analysis Can Remove an Allocation, but Only in Compiled Code and Only While the Object Stays Local

recorded.prompt:q-virtual-xml: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-virtual-xml: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-virtual-xml: Page decides c: 'A virtual thread is still capped' (L116-117) with output 'platform, -Xss default: 9,835 ... virtual: 9,818' and 1,643 vs 1,626 at -Xss256k (L126-134); 'frames are copied to the heap when it unmounts ... but -Xss still caps how deep it can go' (L136-137); Summary 'A virtual thread is capped by -Xss too' (L354). About the same depth is shown directly.
recorded.prompt:q-csv-buffer: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-csv-buffer: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-csv-buffer: Page decides d by the analogous HeapFull case: 'OutOfMemoryError Is Thrown by Whichever Allocation Fails, Not by the Code That Filled the Heap' (L142); the trace names render(), which 'holds nothing after it returns', while the static cache holds the memory (L168-169); 'A smaller buffer in render() would move the failure to the next allocation, and a bigger heap moves it to a later request' (L172-173); Summary L355-356. The stem's static session map maps onto the page's static reportCache.
recorded.prompt:q-cache-36g: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-cache-36g: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-cache-36g: Page decides b: '-Xmx32g: ... UseCompressedOops = false' (L252); 'At -Xmx32g every reference field and object-array slot doubles, so a heap full of collections can hold less data than at -Xmx31g' (L255-256); Reference table '-XX:-UseCompressedOops | 8-byte references; also the default from -Xmx32g up' (L382). The page shows only 31g/32g, not 30g/36g, but 'from -Xmx32g up' (L359, L382) covers 36g.
recorded.prompt:q-window-metrics: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-window-metrics: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-window-metrics: Page decides c: 'The analysis sees only what C2 has inlined. With the record's constructor excluded from inlining ... the Point is passed to a call the compiler can't see into, and counts as escaping' (L302-304), output stays-local 234,375 KB (L308); 'A refactoring that stores the object, or adds a call the JIT doesn't inline, brings the allocation back' (L314-315); Summary L360-361. The stem's megamorphic call is a different cause of non-inlining than the page's dontinline flag, but the page states the rule generally.
recorded.prompt:q-rule-classes: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-rule-classes: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-rule-classes: Page decides d: Metaspace is 'native memory outside the heap. -Xmx doesn't bound it' (L320); 'A cache of generated classes keyed by something that changes on every request ... is the keep case' (L339-341); keep run failed with 'heap in use 3 MB of 1024 MB max' and 'a bigger -Xmx would have changed nothing' (L333, L337-338); class unloaded only when nothing can reach it (L338-339).

recorded.prompt:q-virtual-xml:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-virtual-xml:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-virtual-xml:a: Refuted by '-Xss still caps how deep it can go' (L137) and virtual 9,818 vs platform 9,835 (L127-129). Partly true: frames do go to the heap on unmount (L136), but that does not lift the cap.
recorded.prompt:q-virtual-xml:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-virtual-xml:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-virtual-xml:b: Refuted by L136-137 and Summary 'A virtual thread is capped by -Xss too' (L354); the -Xss256k run lowers the virtual depth to 1,626 (L133), so -Xss does size virtual threads. Partly true: the heap-copy half matches L136.
recorded.prompt:q-virtual-xml:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-virtual-xml:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-virtual-xml:d: Refuted by output: virtual reached 9,818 vs 9,835 platform (L127-129), about the same depth, not a smaller one. The page says unmounted frames 'cost only what is in use' (L136) but never says the running stack stays at a few KB.
recorded.prompt:q-csv-buffer:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-csv-buffer:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-csv-buffer:a: Refuted: 'The stack trace names render(), which holds nothing after it returns' (L168) and the per-call buffer is 'freed when render() returns' (L156); the trace names the allocation that failed, not the holder (L355).
recorded.prompt:q-csv-buffer:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-csv-buffer:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-csv-buffer:b: Refuted: 'The collector frees only objects that nothing reachable refers to' (L183) and the error is thrown only after the buffer 'didn't fit even after a full collection' (L171-172), so being new does not protect anything. Caveat: the page never discusses object age or generations directly; the refutation is by inference from L171-172 and L183. Partly true: the session map holding most of the heap is right.
recorded.prompt:q-csv-buffer:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-csv-buffer:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-csv-buffer:c: Refuted by analogy: a per-call buffer is garbage once the call returns (L52-53, L156, L168). The page says nothing about unflushed buffers specifically, but its rule (garbage once nothing refers to it, L53) covers per-report objects.
recorded.prompt:q-cache-36g:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-cache-36g:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-cache-36g:a: Refuted: the 12-byte header has 'a 4-byte class pointer, compressed by default whether or not references are' (L230-231); the -UseCompressedOops output is 'trimmed to the rows that changed' (L238-239) and new Object()/one int are not among them.
recorded.prompt:q-cache-36g:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-cache-36g:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-cache-36g:c: Refuted: entries grow with oops off: one reference 16 -> 24 bytes, String 48 -> 56, ArrayList<Long> 28 -> 32 bytes each (L243-245 vs L219-227); L255-256.
recorded.prompt:q-cache-36g:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-cache-36g:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-cache-36g:d: Refuted: 'A heap that the shifted address can't reach turns them off' (L248) with -Xmx32g false (L252); compressed oops reach 32 GB (L237-238). Depends on heap size, not machine memory.
recorded.prompt:q-window-metrics:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-window-metrics:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-window-metrics:a: Refuted: an object passed to 'a call the compiler can't see into ... counts as escaping' (L303-304); allocation returns (L308, L314-315).
recorded.prompt:q-window-metrics:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-window-metrics:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-window-metrics:b: Refuted: '-XX:+PrintCompilation shows staysLocal compiled at tier 4, by C2, in that run as well: the method is still compiled, and the allocation stays in the compiled code' (L311-312). Partly true: the outcome 'a Window per call' is right; only the reason is wrong.
recorded.prompt:q-window-metrics:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-window-metrics:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-window-metrics:d: Refuted: 'When it can prove that, it drops the object and works with the values of its fields; when it can't, as with the constructor kept out of inlining, the object goes on the heap' (L401-403); dontinline output shows the allocation (L308). The page does not say in so many words that a non-inlined callee receives a real reference, but the result is shown.
recorded.prompt:q-rule-classes:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-rule-classes:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-rule-classes:a: Refuted: class metadata is in Metaspace, 'native memory outside the heap' (L319-320); keep run failed with 3 MB of 1024 MB heap in use (L333); 'a bigger -Xmx would have changed nothing' (L337-338).
recorded.prompt:q-rule-classes:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-rule-classes:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-rule-classes:b: Refuted: 'drop: defined 300,000 classes, 299,159 unloaded' (L334); 'A class is unloaded only when nothing can reach it any more: a hidden class through its Class object' (L338-339). Partly true: the outcome 'fails again after about two days' is right; only the reason is wrong.
recorded.prompt:q-rule-classes:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-rule-classes:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-rule-classes:c: Refuted: '-Xmx doesn't bound it; -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize does, and by default it is unlimited' (L320-321); Reference table (L373).
